subject: HorizonPay – recovery brief & customer action items
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara@horizonpay.com>, HorizonPay Security <security@horizonpay.com>, Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@horizonpay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HorizonPay – recovery brief & customer action items

Hi Sara / HorizonPay team,

Thank you again for your patience while we completed our internal review of the May 11th service degradation that affected model inference latency for a subset of your requests. Attached is a concise RCA (HorizonPay_RCA_20270514.pdf) and a machine-readable timeline (horizonpay_timeline_05112027.csv). Below is a short summary and the concrete actions we're committing to: 

Summary (short):
- What happened: a combination of an overloaded async batching controller and a regression in cache eviction heuristics caused sustained queue growth for requests routed to a specific GPU pool between 02:18–03:06 UTC on 2027-05-11.
- Impact: increased per-request latency (2–8x) for ~7% of HorizonPay inference traffic; no writes failed, and we observed no errors in model outputs.
- Data exposure risk: our initial review shows no evidence of data exfiltration — requests stayed within the serving tier. We will provide full request audit logs on the cadence below.

Immediate actions (owner / ETA):
- Engineering hotfix to stabilize eviction policy (Dylan Brooks) — deployed 2027-05-12 22:45 UTC (complete).
- Rollback of the batching controller change to default stable policy while we validate (Dylan Brooks) — deployed 2027-05-12 23:10 UTC (complete).
- Additional telemetry and alert thresholds for queue growth across pools (Jonas Weber) — in progress; delivery by 2027-05-20.
- Complete request-level audit package and share with HorizonPay Security (Grace O'Connor) — ETA 2027-05-18.

Planned next steps:
1) We propose a technical readout call next week to walk the timeline and mitigation steps with your security and platform teams.
2) We'll provide the full audit bundle (logs, preserved KV cache snapshots, and scheduler traces) by 2027-05-18.
3) We'll run a follow-up chaos test schedule with you to validate the improved thresholds before returning to the newer batching controller (if you choose).

Attachments: HorizonPay_RCA_20270514.pdf (summary + detailed timeline + mitigation plan), horizonpay_timeline_05112027.csv (event-level timestamps).

If you'd like an earlier call, I can coordinate.

Apologies again for the disruption. We're treating this as a high priority and will keep you closely updated.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

--Attachment stub: HorizonPay_RCA_20270514.pdf (6 pages)
--Attachment stub: horizonpay_timeline_05112027.csv (CSV, 46 rows)
From: Sara Lin <sara@horizonpay.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: HorizonPay Security <security@horizonpay.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HorizonPay – recovery brief & customer action items

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick summary and the attachments. A few clarifying questions from our security team: 
- Can you confirm whether request payloads or any cached artifacts were ever written to persistent storage outside the serving tier?
- Please confirm the exact log range you will provide (request IDs + timestamps) and the retention window.
- We'd also like a copy of the scheduler traces and the patch that caused the eviction regression.

Would you be able to share the audit bundle before EOD Tuesday (our time)? Also please propose 2x slots for the readout (preferably early next week).

Thanks,
Sara
Senior SecOps Engineer, HorizonPay
sara@horizonpay.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, HorizonPay Security <security@horizonpay.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HorizonPay – recovery brief & customer action items

Grace / Sara,

Thanks — apologies for the slow follow-up. Below are the direct answers and what we are delivering in the audit bundle.

Immediate clarifications: 
- Persistent storage: No request payloads or derived cache artifacts were written to any persistent store outside of the serving tier. All cached KV entries were in-memory and discarded when the eviction policy ran.
- Log range: We will provide request-level logs for 2027-05-11 01:45:00 UTC through 2027-05-11 04:00:00 UTC. This includes request IDs, route metadata, pooled GPU id, and per-step latency.
- Scheduler/traces: We are including scheduler traces covering the same window plus 15 minutes before and after (see attached horizonpay_timeline_05112027.csv and mitigation_playbook_v1.md).
- Patch diff: The regression was introduced by change set cd3f7a2; diff is attached (excerpt included in mitigation_playbook_v1.md).

Audit bundle contents (what you'll see in the Drive link):
- request_logs_20270511.gz (parquet) — redacted PII as requested
- scheduler_traces_20270511.trace — human-readable timeline + event ids
- eviction_diff_cd3f7a2.diff — patch for review
- horizonpay_timeline_05112027.csv — event-level timeline we produced for the RCA

Statement on exposure: based on current evidence and our code review, there was no data exfiltration or persistent writes outside the serving layer. We will include hashes of the provided artifacts for your verification.

Next operational steps we will take and timing:
- Full audit bundle upload (Drive link + hashes) — 2027-05-18 09:00 UTC (planned).
- Telemetry thresholds and alerting (Jonas) — 2027-05-20.
- Post-deployment validation window + coordinated rerun of the new batching controller under limit tests — week of 2027-05-24 (proposed).

If you'd like the team to walk through the scheduler traces in a live readout, we can schedule a 60-minute technical session.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime + Orchestration
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

--Attachment stub: horizonpay_timeline_05112027.csv (CSV, 46 rows)
--Attachment stub: mitigation_playbook_v1.md (Markdown, 12 sections)
